claim.quote: DM-Ice17 data are consistent with no modulation in the energy range of 4-20 keV, providing the strongest limits on weakly interacting massive particle dark matter from a direct detection experiment located in the Southern Hemisphere.

key_value_text.note: The result is a null: the abstract gives no modulation amplitude, and the WIMP limit it reports is the 90% C.L. exclusion curve of Fig. 5 (PDF page 5), so `key_value` stays empty. The 'total exposure of 60.8 kg yr' of the abstract, which the record used as its key value until 2026-10-29, is in `summary.technical`.
key_value_text.quote: DM-Ice17 data are consistent with no modulation in the energy range of 4-20 keV
key_value_text.value: DM-Ice17 data are consistent with no annual modulation in the 4-20 keV energy range.

name: First search for a dark matter annual modulation signal with NaI(Tl) in the Southern Hemisphere by DM-Ice17

summary.plain: The first search for a yearly dark matter modulation with sodium iodide in the Southern Hemisphere: 3.6 years of DM-Ice17 data show no modulation between 4 and 20 keV, giving the strongest limits so far from any Southern Hemisphere detector.
summary.technical: Primary physics run 16 June 2011 - 28 January 2015, exposure 60.8 kg yr: data consistent with no modulation in 4-20 keV; limits on WIMP dark matter, the strongest from a Southern Hemisphere direct detection experiment (Phys. Rev. D 95, 032006).

title: First search for a dark matter annual modulation signal with NaI(Tl) in the Southern Hemisphere by DM-Ice17
why_it_matters: The paper says the stable long-term operation shows the South Pole ice is viable for a high-sensitivity NaI(Tl) experiment to test the DAMA/LIBRA claim.
